discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators (the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological band insulators)
motivation: Kane and Mele showed in 2005 that spin-orbit coupling can make a time-reversal-invariant insulator topologically distinct from ordinary insulators. They introduced the Z2 invariant and predicted the quantum spin Hall state with protected helical edge channels. In 2007 Molenkamp's group grew high-quality HgTe/CdTe quantum wells and measured quantized edge conductance, the first realisation of a topological insulator phase. This work moved band topology from the special setting of the quantum Hall effect, which needs strong magnetic fields, into ordinary crystals at zero field. It led to the discovery of three-dimensional topological insulators such as Bi2Se3, topological superconductivity proposals, Weyl semimetals and magnetic topological materials. It changed how the community thinks about materials: every band structure is now classified by its topology. It is a model case of a new organising principle confirmed in real, engineered materials.
